items.text: Subscribers per 1,000 views read 0.6 against a usual 2.8, the one fragile check. In E8, DesignerTom gained 26 subscribers and Dive Club 12, at 9.2 and 3.6 per 1,000 views.
items.recommendation: Add one spoken subscribe ask right after the strongest segment and repeat it in a pinned comment on both channels. Treat Dive Club as the test, since E8 converted there at 3.6 per 1,000 views versus 9.2 on DesignerTom.

items.text: Announce posts earn plays at 25.2, still under the usual 32. E5, a soft launch, drew 1,127 YouTube views at its launch read where the episodes around it typically had 1,751.
items.recommendation: Rewrite the next announce around one named guest and a 30-second clip, post it on both channels a day ahead, and compare its play rate with this week's 25.2 to see if the change helped.

items.text: Viewers leave early: in E5, 5.3 of every 100 left about an eighth of the way in, during a personal story. In E9, 5.1 left at the same point, during talk about nominations.
items.recommendation: Test moving the first guest or demo into the opening quarter-hour of the next episode and trimming catch-up chat before it. Then check whether the early exits shrink.

items.text: Search and suggested videos bring 13.5 of every 100 YouTube views, under the usual 14.7 and softening. Subscribers supply 71.7 of every 100; end screens delivered 19 views and Shorts 6.
items.recommendation: Put the guest's name and the tool in the next title and add chapters. Cut 2 short clips from the strongest moments for Shorts and point end screens at the newest episode. Change one thing at a time.

items.text: E9 had 109 average live viewers, 275 chat messages and 73 people chatting. E12 had 86 average viewers, 138 messages and 67 chatters, so the chat has thinned.
items.recommendation: Test bringing back viewer submissions and a soundboard moment like E9's, and check caller audio before going live, since LinkedIn viewers once said they couldn't hear a caller.
